result.rationale: The diff's delete action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` with no `.catch`, in contrast to the adjacent save action which explicitly uses `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. A rejected destroyRecord promise would be unhandled, so a failed DELETE leaves the admin with no visible feedback while the host row remains; the observable asymmetry within this diff confirms the mechanism.

judged_text: The delete action calls host.destroyRecord().then(...) with no .catch, so a failed DELETE (stale id, expired session, network error) is an unhandled rejection that surfaces no error to the admin. An admin who confirms deletion while the request fails sees no error dialog and the row silently stays in the table (or, on a double-confirm, the second request 500s invisibly), leaving no signal that the host was not deleted; the failure appears only in the browser console, unlike the save path which pops up popupAjaxError.
